entries.summary: Integer addition is laundered through float64 (value/ops.go:37-72), so operands above 2^53 lose precision; Rust does checked i128 arithmetic.

At the i64 edge Rust promotes past i64::MAX (i128) while the Go port's float64 round-trip lands on an i64 boundary value. The Go result is architecture-dependent: darwin/arm64 saturates to math.MaxInt64, linux/amd64 wraps to math.MinInt64 -- the platform-dependent int64(float64) conversion the scope predicted.
Remainder sign: Rust minijinja returns the Euclidean remainder 1 for -7 % 2; Go's math.Mod returns -1.
Rust divides as float and renders inf for 1/0; the Go port raises an invalid-operation error. The whole outcome category differs, not just the bytes.
Containment coercion: Rust stringifies the left operand for a string container, so 1 in '1' is true; the Go port only matches string operands.
Rust str::to_lowercase applies full Unicode case mapping, lowering U+0130 to i + U+0307; Go's strings.ToLower applies simple per-rune mapping and drops the combining dot.
Rust str::to_uppercase expands U+00DF to SS; Go's per-rune uppercase leaves it unchanged.
BAML builds the engine with preserve_order so maps display in insertion order; the Go port's map value sorts keys (value/value.go:936-946).
The same ordering difference observed through iteration: rendered prompt bytes depend on map order, so this is not display-only.
The #597 enum fence in generic form. BoundaryML's engine delta asks an object's value_cmp before ordinary equality; the fork has no such hook, only object-to-object ObjectCmp.

entries.summary: urlencode is a Go-port default (defaults.go:13-130) but BAML does not enable the urlencode feature, so the engine rejects it. A Go-only extra must not become a supported BAML behaviour.
